mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.0% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the tightening phase (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a labor market softening without cost-push inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market moderation without inflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the combined signal (p < 0.05), or the pattern reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it indicates strengthening economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive when INDPRO exceeds the 2% threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects weakening construction activity and reduced economic capacity.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite two consecutive monthly declines in HOUST (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased consumer confidence and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% after two consecutive months at or above 4.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the low-unemployment regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales (implied via PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) suggests robust demand, which precedes a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and INDPRO both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies rise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for three consecutive months in a labor slack regime is expected to produce a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to deflationary pressure.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during the three-month deflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly RSAFS (reserves) series above 350 billion dollars indicates excess liquidity, which is associated with a positive S&P 5-day forward return as markets anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when RSAFS exceeds 350B (p > 0.05).
